message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this a definite STEMI from the image, but I wouldn’t use it to rule out a heart attack.**

I see a regular sinus rhythm around 80 bpm, narrow QRS complexes, and prominent T waves in V3–V4 with subtle ST-segment changes. I don’t see unequivocal ST elevation meeting standard STEMI criteria. However, acute coronary blockage can occur without those criteria. [ACC/AHA guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If there is current or recent chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, call emergency services now and don’t drive yourself.** This needs prompt clinical review, comparison with previous ECGs, repeat ECGs, and troponin testing.

What symptoms prompted this ECG, when did they start, and what is the person’s age?
